records.kind: statutory arrangement letting the government set the bank's exchange rate policy
records.summary: Under section 29 of the Bank of Guyana Act, Chapter 85:02 (Act No. 19 of 1998, enacted 31 December 1998), the Minister, in consultation with the Bank, specifies the policies, principles and criteria of Guyana's exchange rate system, and the Bank is responsible only for the day-to-day administration of that system. Section 14(2) of the same Act lets the President terminate the appointment of the Governor, and the Minister terminate the appointment of any other Director, on stated grounds. Section 3(1) describes the Bank as an autonomous institution governed by the Act. This record rests on the consolidated text of the Act published by Guyana's Ministry of Legal Affairs.
records.source_title: Laws of Guyana, Volume 16, Chapters 83.01-89.01: Bank of Guyana Act, Cap. 85:02 (Ministry of Legal Affairs, Guyana)

records.kind: statutory arrangement letting the executive overrule and remove the bank's board
records.summary: Article 197 of the Constitution of Uruguay provides that where the Poder Ejecutivo considers the management or acts of the Directores of an ente autonomo inconvenient or unlawful it may make observations and suspend the acts observed, and that if the observations are disregarded it may order the rectifications, correctives or removals it sees fit, reporting them to the Senate. Article 198 adds that the Poder Ejecutivo may remove board members with the Senate's consent for ineptitude, omission or crime in office, that if the Senate does not rule within sixty days the Poder Ejecutivo may make the removal effective, and that such removals give no right of appeal to the Tribunal de lo Contencioso Administrativo. The Banco Central del Uruguay is an ente autonomo, and article 14 of its charter designates its directors under article 187 of this same chapter.
records.source_title: Constitucion de la Republica de Uruguay, Seccion XI, Capitulo I (Justia Uruguay)
records.quote: el Poder Ejecutivo podra disponer las rectificaciones, los correctivos o remociones que considere del caso

parties.role: may suspend the board's acts and order rectifications, correctives or removals

records.summary: Two 2004 internal audits of the Bank of Canada, released under the Access to Information Act, criticised the bank for slack financial practices. The audits found that employees of the central bank paid invoices without authorization, did not evaluate whether they got good value from suppliers, and violated a fail-safe system meant to guard against cheque fraud. One of the reports is dated 15 October.
